name: Padua score
seoTitle: Padua score Calculator: Free, With Steps
seoDesc: Padua score: a free health calculator that walks you through 12 values, with the formula spelled out and a worked example.
summary:
The Padua score calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports the result immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer.

Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Padua score calculator work?
sections.html:
The Padua score calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you type in the padua score.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
What you supply, field by field
FieldUnits and meaning
Agea single on/off switch — tick it for “Age ≥ 70 years”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Reduced mobilitya single on/off switch — tick it for “Reduced mobility”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Hormonal treatmenta single on/off switch — tick it for “Ongoing hormonal treatment”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Active cancera single on/off switch — tick it for “Active Cancer — ongoing malignant process”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Trauma surgerya single on/off switch — tick it for “Trauma / surgery within last month”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Previous VTEa single on/off switch — tick it for “History of venous thromboembolism — e.g., DVT (deep vein thrombosis), Budd-Chiari syndrome, pulmonary embolism. With exclusion of superficial vein thrombosis!”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Thrombophilic conditiona single on/off switch — tick it for “Known thrombophilic condition — increased coagulability, e.g., factor V Leiden mutation, antiphospholipid syndrome”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Failurea single on/off switch — tick it for “Heart failure / Respiratory failure — heart attack or a stroke caused by the arteries blockage”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Myocardial infractiona single on/off switch — tick it for “Myocardial infraction / Ischemic stroke”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Infectiona single on/off switch — tick it for “Acute infection / Rheumatologic disease — e.g., lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
Padua scorea number, expressed in points.

11 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Padua score calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Obesity=-active cancer − age − failure − hormonal treatment − infection − myocardial infraction − previous VTE − reduced mobility + padua score − thrombophilic condition − trauma surgery

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• The option the calculation settles on.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Padua score calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Padua score calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 11 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (11 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Padua score = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Padua score calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
